Article Title: 'Character assassination must stop': Kangana slams targeting of Tamil Nadu actress 'for her relations'
Article Text:
Kangana said women, particularly those in positions of power and authority, are often targeted.

NEW DELHI: Actor-turned-politician Kangana Ranaut said "character assassination of women" must stop, calling on society to examine its attitude towards women. She said women, particularly those in positions of power and authority, are often targeted through attacks on their character in an attempt to undermine them."We all know that this is not restricted to India alone and is prevalent worldwide that character of working women, successful women, actors, politicians, women at the position of power and authority is targeted to bring her down," Ranaut told reporters after chairing the District Development Coordination and Monitoring meeting at Kullu on Monday.The BJP MP's remarks came when she was asked about Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's recent speech in which he warned against personal attacks, double-meaning insults and derogatory remarks targeting women.Ranaut, who played former Tamil Nadu chief minister J Jayalalithaa in the 2021 biopic Thalaivii, referred to the alleged humiliation Jayalalithaa faced in the Tamil Nadu Assembly."In Tamil Nadu, we have seen that a very renowned actress was targeted for her relations," she said, adding that relations are from both sides but only the woman is targeted for abuse, "cheer haran" (disrobing) and character assassination."We as a society should look into our self that how do we look at women and do we really respect them or not,” she added.Vijay, in his speech in the Tamil Nadu Assembly, criticised derogatory political remarks against women and invoked the alleged abuse and humiliation faced by Jayalalithaa during the 1989 Assembly episode.His remarks came amid a recent controversy over comments attributed to DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin concerning actor Trisha , an issue whose interpretation has been disputed by the DMK.The Assembly also witnessed ruckus on Tuesday after the DMK objected to Vijay's remarks and demanded that references based on Enforcement Directorate documents be expunged from the records.Opposition MLAs raised slogans and were evicted from the House.The confrontation began after Vijay, while speaking on the Home Department and law and order, criticised the previous DMK government, citing ED material, the Sarkaria Commission and alleged corruption during earlier regimes.Udhayanidhi sought permission to respond to the allegations, but the Speaker did not allow an immediate reply amid disruptions, prompting the DMK to stage a walkout.
Article Summary: Kangana Ranaut said women, particularly those in positions of power and authority, are often targeted through attacks on their character. The BJP MP's remarks came when she was asked about Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's recent speech in which he warned against personal attacks, double-meaning insults.

Article Title: 'To stop love jihad': Maharashtra minister Nitesh Rane backs VHP's call to bar Muslims from Navratri events
Article Text:
Maharashtra inister Nitesh Rane (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra minister Nitesh Rane expressed support for the Vishva Hindu Parishad 's (VHP) call to bar Muslims from the Navratri events in the state, alleging that otherwise this would lead to an increase in "love jihad" cases.Attendees at such festivities should undergo identity checks and recite the Hanuman Chalisa before entry, the BJP leader told PTI Videos on Monday."Love jihad" is a term used by right-wing activists to allege a ploy by Muslim men to lure women (mostly from the Hindu community) into relationships for religious conversion."Those who do not follow idol worship should not participate in Hindu religious events. Those coming for garba should show their identity and chant the Hanuman Chalisa before being allowed entry," Rane said, extending support to the VHP's demand.The VHP last week announced that Muslims "would not be allowed" entry to garba and dandiya venues across the state during the upcoming Navratri festival, and issued "guidelines" for organisers to verify participants' identities by checking their Aadhaar cards and applying tilak on their foreheads.The Navratri festival will begin on October 11.On the demand to curb DJ sound systems during the upcoming Ganesh festival, Rane called for the rules to be applied uniformly to all religious processions.“If DJs are not permitted during Ganesh festival celebrations, similar restrictions should apply to Eid processions as well,” he said.Rane alleged that loud music was played late into the night during recent Eid processions, adding that Hindus follow court orders and noise regulations.He also slammed Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray over his reported remarks about alleged vulgar dances during Kanwar Yatra events in parts of Uttar Pradesh, questioning why criticism was directed only at Hindu practices while statements by Muslim clerics were not similarly discussed.The BJP minister asserted that some people were attempting to "defame" Hinduism and Sanatan Dharma.
Article Summary: Nitesh Rane supports Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) call to bar Muslims from Navratri events. VHP last week announced that Muslims "would not be allowed" entry to garba and dandiya venues across the state. Rane: Those who do not follow idol worship should not participate in Hindu religious events.

Article Title: DMK MLAs evicted from TN assembly after ruckus over CM Vijay's remarks
Article Text:
Speaker JCD Prabhakar refused to accept DMK's demand to expunge CM Vijay's remark from assembly records

DMK legislators were bundled out of the Tamil Nadu assembly on Tuesday following intense protests demanding the expunging of Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s remarks regarding former Chief Minister M Karunanidhi, late Union Minister Murasoli Maran, the Sarkaria Commission, and ED dossiers in recent cases.The situation turned chaotic after Speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge the remarks, ruling that Vijay had merely cited the Sarkaria Commission, which had been discussed at length in the House previously. Declaring that there was no need to expunge the remarks, the Speaker gave his ruling, triggering further escalation as DMK members upped the ante, raised slogans, and brought the proceedings to a standstill by sitting in the well of the House.The Speaker urged the protesting members to return to their seats, offering to allow DMK whip E V Velu and deputy leader of the opposition K N Nehru to speak on the issue. However, the DMK members refused to yield and continued their agitation."I will not reverse my ruling," Speaker Prabhakar asserted before ordering the marshals to remove the unyielding members. He also cautioned Kallakurichi MLA Vasantham K Karthikeyan against approaching the chair.Marshals subsequently entered the House and physically removed the protesting MLAs, carrying out members including Kutty (Valparai), Durai Chandrasekaran (Thiruvaiyaru), Vasantham Karthikeyan (Rishivandiyam) and a few more who refused to budge from the well. The disruption halted assembly proceedings around 10:03 am, following earlier heated exchanges between former ministers Velu and Nehru and ministers Aadhav Arjuna and R Nirmalkumar.
Article Summary: DMK legislators were bundled out of the Tamil Nadu assembly on Tuesday following intense protests. They were demanding the expunging of Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s remarks regarding former Chief Minister M Karunanidhi, late Union Minister Murasoli Maran, the Sarkaria Commission, and ED dossiers in recent cases. The situation turned chaotic after Speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge the remarks.

Article Title: Delhi building collapse: SC appointed amicus curiae seeks safety audit of PGs, hostels across capital
Article Text:
6 killed in Satya Niketan building collapse; FIR against owner

NEW DELHI: A Supreme Court-appointed amicus curiae on Wednesday filed a report before the top court on the building collapse in Satya Niketan and requested the apex court to direct its appointed committee to carry out inspections and safety audits of all PG accommodations, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments situated in and around colleges and universities across Delhi.Senior advocate Ajit Kumar Sinha, in his report, said that the Satya Niketan incident assumes significance as the locality had witnessed another building collapse in April 2022, in which two people were killed and four injured.“The present incident is also required to be viewed in the context of an earlier building collapse in Satya Niketan in April 2022, in which two persons lost their lives, and four others were injured. The recurrence of such an incident in the same locality raises serious concerns regarding the effectiveness of the existing mechanism for inspection, identification of dangerous structures, and enforcement of building bye-laws”, the amicus report said.He also noted that construction-related work was being undertaken in or around the basement and that there were reports of waterlogging in the basement immediately before the latest collapse.The amicus has sought a time-bound inspection and safety audit of PGs, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments around colleges and universities across Delhi, including checks on sanctioned building plans, actual construction and number of floors, basement construction and alterations, land use, structural and fire safety, ingress and egress, and dangerous or ruinous conditions.This comes after seven people were killed when a building collapsed in Satya Niketan on Sunday.Meanwhile, Municipal Corporation of Delhi also directed its executive engineers (building) across all zones to inspect structures under their jurisdiction and submit comprehensive reports by September 10, following the deadly building collapse in south Delhi's Satya Niketan, which killed seven people, officials said.Officials said the information collected during the inspections would be incorporated into an affidavit to be filed before the Delhi High Court within 10 days.The inspections and submission of reports will be personally monitored and supervised by the additional commissioners concerned in each zone, according to the order, they added.
Article Summary: A Supreme Court-appointed amicus curiae filed a report before the top court on the building collapse in Satya Niketan. He requested the apex court to direct its appointed committee to carry out inspections and safety audits of all PG accommodations, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments situated in and around colleges and universities.

BRS protests over 1,000 days of Congress rule

NEW DELHI: A video showing a security official pulling the hair of BRS MLA and former Telangana minister Sabitha Indra Reddy during a protest outside the state assembly in Hyderabad has triggered a political row.The incident took place on Monday as Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) legislators protested against the Congress-led government, alleging that it had failed to fulfil its election promises even after completing 1,000 days in office.Visuals shared by the BRS on X purportedly show security personnel trying to remove Sabitha Indra Reddy from the protest site. During the confrontation, a security official is seen pulling her by her hair as she is taken away from the assembly premises. The BRS alleged that the MLA was dragged away despite being a woman legislator.In its post on X, the BRS said, "Police's inhuman behavior towards former minister and MLA Sabeeta Indra Reddy at the assembly! Police dragging her away brutally by her hair without even considering that she is a woman MLA! Is this the respect the Congress government gives to women?"The incident occurred amid heightened tensions outside the Telangana assembly on the opening day of its monsoon session.BRS legislators and MLCs had arrived wearing black T-shirts carrying slogans targeting the Congress government's performance after 1,000 days in power. The party has accused the ruling government of failing to deliver on its election promises.The legislators attempted to enter the assembly premises but were stopped by security personnel. The ensuing confrontation led to pushing and jostling between BRS members and police.BRS working president KT Rama Rao, former minister T Harish Rao and several other party leaders were detained after being stopped from entering the assembly. They were later shifted away from the protest site.Police, however, said the legislators were stopped because of slogans printed on their black T-shirts and that officers were acting on the instructions of the assembly Speaker. A senior police official said allegations of misconduct would be examined using video footage.The BRS has condemned the action and said it would raise the issue with the assembly Speaker.

NEW DELHI: Taking note of another instance of a Shiv Sena politician in Maharashtra assaulting doctors, Supreme Court Monday said the situation in the state had worsened and favoured strict action against politicians to send a message that such behaviour against a medical practitioner would not be tolerated.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said people indulging in violence against doctors should be arrested without any delay. "They do not deserve to roam around," the bench said while referring to the recent incident of Sena workers assaulting doctors and hospital staff in Palghar.SC made the observations while hearing the plea of Sena corporator Ramesh Sukrya Mhatre, who is accused of assaulting doctors at Dombivli in July. He had moved SC against stringent conditions imposed by HC on him while granting bail last month. Sensing the mood of the court, senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi sought to withdraw the petition.The court allowed his plea for the withdrawal but before that, it expressed its concern over the growing number of incidents of doctors being attacked by politicians and said that it cannot be justified.Rohatgi said the group of people responsible for the assault in Palghar was different, but SC said they belonged to the same party. "Same ideology. How can this be justified that you go and assault them inside their chambers and beat them brutally? It's an issue of law and public order," the bench said. Mhatre was arrested in July for allegedly assaulting doctors and staff at a civic-run hospital in Dombivli on July 6.
Article Summary: Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said people indulging in violence against doctors should be arrested without any delay. Article Title: IIT Mandi orders inquiry after poster says Shudras should ‘serve higher classes’
Article Text:
Controversial caste poster at IIT Mandi sparks row, institute orders inquiry into display

Director distances institute from poster

What the controversial poster said

Behera's Gita and ISKCON links

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: IIT Mandi has set up an inquiry after a Bhagavad Gita-themed poster displayed on its campus during Janmashtami celebrations described Shudras as being meant to "serve higher classes", triggering controversy over caste discrimination.Institute Director Laxmidhar Behera said the poster was part of a student-led event and had not been approved by the institute. He said he was "shocked" when he learnt about the display and stressed that IIT Mandi does not support caste-based discrimination.In an email to the IIT Mandi community on Sunday, Behera described the development as an "Outright condemnation of recent poster display within campus". He said the poster, displayed on September 4, had not been endorsed by the institute "in any manner"."I have personally fought against caste-based discrimination in any form in every forum. I have instituted an enquiry committee in this matter such that the institute campus is never used for any such violation of social harmony. I fully empathise with members of our community who have been hurt by this incident," he wrote.Behera said IIT Mandi was committed to "the values of equality, social justice, scientific temper" and the principles laid down in the Constitution."The institute strongly condemns any form of caste based discrimination," he said, urging members of the campus community to "stand together against such biases/discrimination in any form".Speaking to PTI, Behera said the poster had been prepared for a student event. He said the inquiry committee included faculty members and representatives from different social categories, including members of the Scheduled Castes and Other Backward Classes.The poster, titled "Bhagavad Gita - The Timeless Wisdom", was put up outside the institute's auditorium during Janmashtami celebrations.It divided society into four groups mentioned in the Bhagavad Gita, namely Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras. It described Brahmanas as those who "spread God's message", Kshatriyas as those who "protect society and spirituality" and Vaishyas as those who "drive economy, support others".For Shudras, however, the poster listed their role as "serve higher classes", which became the focus of the controversy.The poster also quoted a Bhagavad Gita verse stating that the four divisions of human society were created according to the "three modes of material nature and the work associated with them".Behera said he had been away from IIT Mandi and returned on Saturday. He said he learnt about the controversy on Sunday morning."I have not seen the poster. I don't want to take a side here and let the panel decide," he told PTI.The controversy has also drawn attention to Behera's long association with the Bhagavad Gita and ISKCON.According to his official IIT Mandi profile, Behera has spent 27 years teaching what he describes as the "universal principles of peace through Bhagavad Gita". He is also known as "HG Lila Purushottam Das" and is the founder of the proposed Bhaktivedanta University, whose website describes it as an ISKCON initiative.Behera currently teaches a three-credit course on the Bhagavad Gita at IIT Mandi.He defended ISKCON's position on caste, saying the organisation opposes discrimination and promotes equality."ISKCON is the only organisation that strictly and strongly speaks against caste-based discrimination. In ISKCON, pujaris are also from the Shudra community. Muslims are also pujaris," he claimed."We are against casteism in all forms. All occupational duties are according to guna and karma," he added.Behera also highlighted what he said was increased representation of marginalised communities at IIT Mandi during his tenure. According to him, the institute had no OBC, SC or ST faculty members when he joined, while their numbers have since risen substantially. The IIT director has previously faced criticism over his public views.In 2023, he asked students to take a pledge against eating meat and linked landslides and cloudbursts in Himachal Pradesh to cruelty towards animals. In 2022, shortly after becoming IIT Mandi director, a video surfaced in which he claimed to have helped a friend's family get rid of "evil spirits" through chanting holy mantras.More recently, IIT Mandi's Indian Knowledge System and Mental Health Applications Centre held a conference in June that included sessions on the Bhagavad Gita, Ayurveda and reincarnation. Behera was among its general chairs and co-organised a session titled "Reincarnation, OBEs and afterlife communication".The institute's inquiry committee will now examine how the poster was prepared, displayed and presented during the student-led event.
Article Summary: IIT Mandi sets up inquiry after Bhagavad Gita-themed poster sparks controversy. Poster described Shudras as being meant to "serve higher classes" Institute Director Laxmidhar Behera said the poster was part of a student-led event. He said he was "shocked" when he learnt about the display and stressed that IITMandi does not support caste-based discrimination.

Article Title: Watch: CCTV captures moment Delhi's Satya Niketan building collapsed, leaving 6 dead
Article Text:
The CCTV footage showed the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road

10 patients taken to Trauma Centre

MCD orders demolition of dangerous building

NEW DELHI: CCTV footage has captured the moment a multi-storey building collapsed in Delhi's Satya Niketan area, killing six people and triggering a major rescue operation.The building, which housed a boys' paying guest accommodation near Delhi University's South Campus, collapsed around 1.30 pm on Sunday while repair and construction work was underway. The death toll rose to six after one more person rescued during the night was declared dead.The CCTV footage showed the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road. Rescue and search operations continued through the night as teams searched the rubble for anyone who may still be trapped.Multiple agencies, including the Delhi Police, Delhi Fire Service, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Delhi Disaster Management Authority, have been involved in the operation."One more person was rescued during the night but was brought dead, taking the toll to six," Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southwest) Amit Goel said, PTI reported.Police have registered a case against the building owner and others, while a magisterial inquiry has also been ordered. Officials are continuing efforts to trace people allegedly connected with the incident.To the residents, the collapse felt like a quake. “We felt the ground shake.When we ran outside, we saw that a house had completely collapsed,” said Roshan Pal, a student from Lucknow.“When I came out, a cloud of dust was spreading in all directions. That’s when we realised that the building had collapsed. We started removing one part of a wall soon after. Seven students were under it,” said Rahul Gaur, a resident, TOI reported.According to AIIMS, the JPN Apex Trauma Centre received 10 patients injured in the building collapse. Of the 10 patients, five were brought dead, while another patient who was in critical condition later succumbed to injuries.Three patients have been admitted and are undergoing treatment. One of them underwent limb surgery, while another patient with minor injuries was discharged after observation.Investigators are examining whether construction work carried out in the basement may have contributed to the collapse.Initial inquiries suggested that the basement was prone to waterlogging, which may have weakened the structure. Investigators are now examining whether construction work aggravated the situation and contributed to the collapse.The MCD is also looking into the matter. Similar concerns over basement work, water accumulation and the structural condition of the building have emerged in the preliminary probe.Police are likely to examine whether permission had been obtained for the work and why construction was being carried out during the monsoon, sources said. "The building owner, contractor and labourers will be interrogated," an investigator said, TOI reported.It was not immediately clear whether the building owner had obtained permission for the construction or whether the work was being carried out illegally, allegedly in connivance with local authorities.According to the MCD, the premises of Building/House No. 13, Satya Niketan, New Delhi, was found to be in a "ruinous, dangerous condition" and posed a threat to people occupying, visiting or passing by the building as well as those in the neighbourhood.Under Section 348 of the DMC Act, 1957, read with Section 491 of the Act, the MCD has ordered the property to be demolished within three days of receipt of the order.The order said that if the owner fails to comply within the specified period, the MCD will demolish the building and recover the demolition charges as arrears of tax.The collapse has raised fresh questions over the safety of buildings being used as paying guest accommodations and the enforcement of construction and fire safety norms in densely populated areas of Delhi.Congress leader and AICC Uttarakhand in-charge Kumari Selja questioned the BJP government over the safety of students living in such accommodations.“What is the BJP government doing? They have forgotten what happened at the coaching centre. A mafia is operating in Delhi. These children are sent away with so many hopes. They are the only support for their parents. Who is responsible for their safety?” Selja said.Former Delhi chief secretary Omesh Saigal said the incident should not be viewed in isolation and raised concerns over unauthorised construction in parts of the capital."Look at the kind of buildings constructed in Delhi—I would say that in some areas, one in five buildings is unauthorised; either the blueprints weren't approved, extra floors were added, or the construction is substandard," he said.Saigal also called for restrictions on new construction in areas that are already overcrowded. "At the very least, we should ban new construction in these areas. We must halt new construction or stop sanctioning building plans, for areas that are already over-congested and over-built. These are the things that need to be addressed," he added.
Article Summary: CCTV footage shows the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road. Rescue and search operations continued through the night as teams searched the rubble for anyone who may still be trapped. Police have registered a case against the building owner and others, while a magisterial inquiry has been ordered.

Article Title: ‘Bye-bye, papa’: What 21-year-old told father before jumping into Chenab
Article Text:
The video, which was said to have been recorded by passersby at the bridge, shows people attempting to discourage her. Despite their efforts, she reportedly jumped into the Chenab.

‘This is my own life’

NEW DEHI: A 21-year-old woman allegedly jumped into the Chenab River in Doda district on Saturday after speaking to her father over the phone and telling him, "This is my life," before saying, "Bye-bye, papa. " A joint rescue operation was launched soon after the incident, but there was no immediate trace of her.The incident took place around 2 pm at the Shiva Dal bridge near Prem Nagar. Police, personnel from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and local volunteers joined the search operation in the river after the woman, identified as Payal Devi, reportedly jumped from the bridge.A video purportedly recorded by passersby who attempted to discourage her from taking the step shows Devi saying "bye-bye" before jumping into the Chenab. The video subsequently went viral on social media.Officials said the circumstances that led to Devi taking the extreme step were not immediately known.The final conversation between Devi and her father, Krishan Lal, came shortly before she disappeared into the river.According to Lal, Devi had gone to a mela earlier in the day. She later called him and said that she was feeling unwell and intended to consult a doctor.When the doctor was reportedly unavailable, Devi began making her way back. At some point, she apparently got onto a motorcycle.Lal said he subsequently received a call from a person who was accompanying his daughter. The person told him that Devi had run towards the river.The development prompted Lal to speak to his daughter over the phone. He said he repeatedly asked her what had happened and whether somebody had said or done anything to her.Lal recalled Devi telling him, "Nobody should come near me."He continued trying to understand what had happened and urged her to explain why she was behaving that way.According to Lal, Devi responded, "No, papa. This is my own life. My heart tells me that I should go this way."She then told her father, "Bye-bye, papa," before the call ended, he said.The moments before Devi jumped were also reportedly captured on video.The video, which was said to have been recorded by passersby at the bridge, shows people attempting to discourage her. Despite their efforts, she reportedly jumped into the Chenab.The footage later circulated widely on social media, drawing attention to the incident and the efforts of those present to prevent her from taking the step.Following the incident, police, SDRF personnel and local volunteers launched a joint rescue operation in the Chenab River.Teams searched the river for Devi, but officials said there was no trace of her.The search operation was undertaken after the reported jump from the Shiva Dal bridge, a location near Prem Nagar in Doda district.As the rescue teams continued their efforts, the reasons behind Devi's actions remained unclear. Officials said the circumstances that led to her decision were not immediately known.Her father's account indicates that she had earlier complained of feeling unwell and had intended to see a doctor, but what happened between that conversation and her reported arrival at the bridge remains unclear.The investigation and search operation are continuing, while authorities are attempting to establish the sequence of events leading up to the incident.
Article Summary: Payal Devi, 21, reportedly jumped into the Chenab River in Doda district on Saturday. A video purportedly recorded by passersby shows Devi saying "bye-bye" before jumping into the river. A joint rescue operation was launched soon after the incident, but there was no immediate trace of her.

Article Title: ‘Will reduce UP to Orwellian Dystopia’: Allahabad HC raps Noida DM over student’s NSA detention

Akriti Chaudhary, a 24-year-old Delhi University history graduate and student activist, was arrested in connection with cases arising from a workers’ protest in Noida in April 2026

NEW DELHI: The Allahabad High Court has ordered recovery of Rs 5 lakh from the salaries of the Gautam Buddha Nagar district magistrate and other officials after quashing the National Security Act (NSA) detention of Delhi University student and activist Akriti Chaudhary.The division bench of Justices Atul Sreedharan and Achal Sachdev held that Chaudhary's detention violated her fundamental right to life and personal liberty under Article 21, finding that the material relied upon by authorities did not justify invoking the stringent preventive detention law.The court directed that Rs 5 lakh be paid to Chaudhary as compensation and recovered from the salary of Gautam Buddha Nagar DM Medha Roopam and other officers found responsible, including the SHO who prepared the initial report backing her detention. It also directed that the court's displeasure with the officials be entered in their service records.In a strongly worded September 2 order, the court criticised the manner in which the detention order was passed and warned that continued "despotic" conduct by "errant" bureaucrats could reduce Uttar Pradesh to an "Orwellian Dystopia", reported PTI.Chaudhary, a 24-year-old history graduate, was arrested in connection with cases arising from a workers' protest in Noida in April 2026.The UP Police invoked the NSA against her and activist-journalist Satya Verma on May 13. They were among activists arrested in cases related to the protest seeking higher wages.The court said the police dossier against Chaudhary contained allegations but lacked credible supporting material. It said the DM was required to independently examine the record before deciding whether preventive detention was warranted."The conduct of the Gautam Buddha Nagar DM who passed the impugned order is worthy of derision," the court said.The bench noted that Chaudhary had no previous criminal record and that there was no material showing she had incited violence. It said the circumstances suggested that the detention was intended to make an example of her and discourage others from exercising their right to freedom of speech and expression in support of labourers.The court also questioned the state's version of when Chaudhary was arrested. It recorded that she was taken into custody around 5.30 pm on April 11 at Botanical Garden Metro Station, although the state claimed her arrest took place on April 12.A notice issued under Section 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was cited by the state. However, the notice carried General Diary Entry No. 37, which was generated only at 10.20 am on April 12."Mentioning the GD number in the notice under section 130 of the BNSS reveals that the petitioner was already arrested and the procedure of giving a notice under section 130 of the BNSS was ex post facto the arrest and nothing more than a sham," Justice Sreedharan said."I agree with the view of brother Justice Achal Sachdev that the notice u/s. 130 of the BNSS was prepared after the arrest of the Petitioner and that is the reason why the time of issuance is not mentioned in the notice and its omission is deliberate," he added.The court said preventive detention under the NSA is an exception and cannot be used in place of ordinary criminal law. It described the grounds of Chaudhary's detention as "repetitive, speculative and are only opinion-based", noting the absence of material supporting those conclusions.It also cautioned authorities against treating peaceful public protests as a threat merely because they could potentially lead to a breach of peace."Preventing people from gathering in public spaces or agitating for their rights on the grounds of assumed breach of peace would be throwing the baby out of the bath water," the court said.The bench said the constitutional protection of freedom of speech and expression extends to peaceful gatherings and collective action, and cannot be curtailed merely on the basis of the state's subjective assessment.The court also reminded bureaucrats and police officers that their duty is to the Constitution rather than the political executive, saying that people are the masters in a democracy.It warned that officials who disregard their constitutional oath could come to be seen as an "oppressive vestige of the British Empire", creating an environment of civil unrest.The court said the judiciary could pass "harsh orders" to compensate citizens where official excesses or illegalities infringe upon civil liberties without adequate cause or due process.
Article Summary: Akriti Chaudhary, a 24-year-old history graduate, was arrested in connection with cases arising from a workers’ protest in Noida in April 2026. The Allahabad High Court has ordered recovery of Rs 5 lakh from the salaries of the Gautam Buddha Nagar district magistrate and other officials.

Article Title: ‘Insulting label’: Rahul Gandhi responds to ‘Dimagi Naxal’ attack, accuses PM Modi of ‘silencing and shaming’ critics
Article Text:
This was the first time Rahul responded to PM Modi's 'Dimagi Naxals' jibe.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Rahul Gandhi on Monday joined the “Dimagi Naxal” debate and accused Prime Minister Modi of using such insulting labels to “silence and shame” those who seek accountability from the government. The Lok Sabha leader of the opposition used the Delhi building collapse incident to target the government and Prime Minister Modi and accuse them of lack of accountability.Prime Minister Modi had used the “Dimagi Naxal” phrase for the first time during his Independence Day address from the Red Fort on August 15."We have succeeded in eliminating armed Naxals from the forests and liberating the nation from that crisis. However, while armed Naxals are gone, 'dimagi' (intellectual) Naxals are lurking around," the Prime Minister had then said, referring to the successes achieved in the government's fight against the Naxals."These dimagi Naxals are looking for ways of violence and anarchy. They are resorting to various tactics to drag society to the wrong path. We must identify these dimagi Naxals, isolate them, and steer the nation's youth toward the mainstream effort of transforming India into a developed nation. The challenge of 'dimagi Naxals should not be underestimated' as they used to have presence in "corridors of power", even as advisers in govt committees," PM Modi had said in his address.The Prime Minister’s remarks evoked strong reactions from the opposition leaders. Senior Congress leader and MP P Chidambaram called "Dimagi Naxals" the latest political "abuse" being used by the BJP against its opponents, describing it as a new variant of earlier labels such as "urban Naxals", "Andolanjeevi" and "tukde tukde gang". Chidambaram said that he was “proud to be a dimagi naxal".Aam Aadmi Party national convenor Arvind Kejriwal also claimed he was proud to be a 'dimagi naxal' as he was a 'true patriot' and did not fear the BJP. "According to PM Modi, those who dare to question are 'damagi naxals', who do not fear the BJP. If Bhagat Singh, BR Ambedkar were alive today, then they would also be termed 'dimagi Naxal' according to the prime minister," Kejriwal had then said in a video message.However, the BJP leaders and the NDA allies put up a strong defence of PM Modi’s “Dimagi Naxal” attack and launched a broadside against the opposition leaders, especially the Congress.Union minister Kiren Rijiju later clarified that PM Modi’s remark was not targeted at political rivals but at those forces who try to belittle and diminish the idea of India by undermining the constitutional framework.In a post on X, Kiren Rijiju said: "PM Narendra Modi ji didn't say Opposition leaders as Dimagi Naxals." Union Minister went on to describe who all fall in the category of the remark."Only following are 'Dimagi Naxals': those who support Maoists and reject Indian Constitution, those who stand with separatists and support Article 370 and those who want to cut chicken neck to separate North-East from India," he asserted.But undeterred by the opposition pushback, PM Modi reiterated his attack last Saturday while addressing the centenary celebrations of Delhi University’s Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) and called his “Dimagi naxal” remark a “homoeopathic pill” for critics.“Homoeopathic treatment only aggravates the disease for a short time. As soon as I gave this pill, all the mental Naxals started coming out. But the public is seeing their true colours,” he said.In fact, the Prime Minister went on to extend his attack by using a new phrase, “naraz fufa”.Taking aim at opponents, PM Modi described two kinds of people in the country. One type positively transforms the power of society into the power of the nation. The other becomes a “Naraz Fufa” (angry uncle) on every issue.“Their only dialogue is: What is the need for this? When we were building the world’s largest statue, they said, what is the need for this? They said the same thing about bullet trains, UPI, chips, and the new Parliament. When we built a memorial for the army heroes who died for the country, the uncles came into the field again. But India gave a befitting reply to such uncles.”The Congress reacted sharply again and said PM Modi's use of labels such as "naraaz phoopa" was part of his modus operandi of giving the opposition a new adjective every year to keep his own "failures" hidden.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said, "Narendra Modi ji, yesterday, you visited SRCC at Delhi University. It was an opportunity for dialogue on the country's youth, education, and their future. But alas, instead of facing the youth's questions, the speech turned into yet another political campaign.""Modi ji's Modus Operandi is to suppress questions in a democracy and give the opposition a new adjective every year so that his own failures remain hidden! Naraaz phoopa, Dimagi Naxal, Urban Naxal, Khan Market Gang, Andolan-jeevi, Parjeevi," Kharge said in a post in Hindi on X.Adjectives keep changing, but the Modi government's "anti-people policies" do not change, Kharge said.Now, with Rahul Gandhi also joining the debate, it will be interesting to see how the BJP reacts to his attacks against PM Modi.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Modi had used the “Dimagi Naxal” phrase for the first time during his Independence Day address from the Red Fort on August 15. Rahul Gandhi on Monday accused PM Modi of using such insulting labels to “silence and shame” those who seek accountability.

Article Title: ‘Work day and night’: SC rejects Aravalli panel's extension plea; CJI says it's waiting for his retirement
Article Text:
The panel had asked for 6-month extension to submit report.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

'Unfortunately & inexplicably': Congress reacts

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to give the expert panel examining the definition and protection of the Aravalli Hills another six months to submit its final report, telling it to "work day and night" and complete the exercise by November 30.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana rejected the high-powered committee's request to extend the deadline till February 28, 2027. The court also warned that it would reconstitute the panel if it failed to submit the report within the next two months, news agency PTI reported."Let the panel work day and night to submit a report on the Aravalli issue. If they are unable to do that in two months, we will reconstitute the whole panel," the CJI observed.The court also directed the committee to submit issue-specific interim reports, allowing it to address urgent aspects of the contentious Aravalli definition without waiting for its comprehensive final report.The CJI appeared particularly unimpressed with the timing of the extension request, observing that the committee had sought more time "with the first stroke of the pen" and appeared to be waiting for his retirement.The court further directed the panel to hear all stakeholders, including tribal communities in Rajasthan and Gujarat, before finalising its recommendations. The matter will next be heard on December 2.The committee had sought six additional months, saying it needed more time to undertake a “comprehensive and defensible” assessment of the Aravalli range. Its deadline for submitting the final report was August 31.In its compliance report filed on August 31, the panel said its assessment required the integration of spatial, ecological, geological, hydrological and socio-economic evidence, besides inputs from stakeholders.It said additional time was needed for geospatial assessment, sensitivity analysis, expert examination, field verification and stakeholder validation.The committee also argued that the Aravalli issue could not be resolved through a “single terrain-based criterion or a single source of evidence”.The urgency around the exercise stems from a controversy over how the Aravallis should be defined for regulatory purposes, particularly mining.The Congress expressed disappointment over the Supreme Court’s decision to reject the High Powered Committee’s request for a six-month extension to submit its final report on the Aravallis.Calling the decision “unfortunate and inexplicable”, party leader Jairam Ramesh said the committee’s request for an extension beyond August 31, 2026, was “most justifiable”. Congress maintained that the additional time was necessary for the committee to complete its work and submit a comprehensive report on the ecologically sensitive Aravalli range.
Article Summary: Panel examining definition and protection of Aravalli Hills told to submit report by November 30. Court also warned that it would reconstitute the panel if it failed to submit the report within the next two months. Committee had sought six additional months, saying it needed more time to undertake a “comprehensive and defensible” assessment of the range.

Article Title: 'I apologise': Bengal CM Adhikari after govt ad sparks row over 'distorted' Durga image
Article Text:
"First of all, as the chief minister of the state, I apologise," CM Suvendu said.

Opposition targets BJP government

BJP says mistake should not be politicised

NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday apologised over a government advertisement that showed Goddess Durga with 11 arms instead of the traditional 10, saying those responsible had been cautioned and promising greater care in future.The advertisement appeared in newspapers ahead of a coordination meeting on Durga Puja preparations at Milan Mela Prangan. It carried an image of Durga with an extra arm holding an indistinct object, triggering criticism from opposition leaders."First of all, as the chief minister of the state, I apologise. A defective advertisement was published this morning. I apologise for that. Those who issued the defective advertisement have been cautioned. The government will be more careful about such matters in future," he said.The advertisement was issued to announce the meeting organised by Kolkata Police and the Kolkata Municipal Corporation in collaboration with the state information and cultural affairs department.CPIM leader Shatarup Ghosh was among those who criticised the depiction and took a swipe at the BJP government."Gods gave Durga ten hands and weapons to kill the demon. The BJP government has given her an extra hand," Ghosh said.TMC MLA and spokesperson Kunal Ghosh also objected to the image and raised the issue with the chief minister on X."Honourable chief minister, in the government advertisement, Maa Durga, who is traditionally depicted as 'doshobhuja' (ten-armed), has become 'ekadoshbhuja' (eleven-armed). According to the scriptures, one hand needs to be removed," wrote TMC spokesperson Kunal Ghosh on X.He posted a picture of the advertisement, which also featured photographs of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Adhikari alongside the image of Goddess Durga."We hear about various codes of conduct every day. If the number of the Mother's arms increases in 2026, the matter could become complicated. Please immediately instruct the department concerned not to distort the original depiction of the Mother Goddess," he added.BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya said the problem appeared to have originated with the agency responsible for designing and publishing the advertisement."It can be corrected. The matter should not be politicised," Bhattacharya said when asked about the controversy.The controversy surfaced as the BJP government prepares to oversee its first Durga Puja in West Bengal, with the administration stressing the traditional character of the festival.Theme-based Puja celebrations were also discussed at Monday's meeting. Adhikari said organisers would be free to use themes but warned them against choosing concepts that could hurt religious or cultural sentiments or undermine Sanatan traditions.The government has said the coordination meeting was intended to help ensure that Durga Puja, West Bengal's biggest annual cultural celebration, is conducted safely and peacefully.
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday apologised over a government advertisement that showed Goddess Durga with 11 arms instead of the traditional 10. The advertisement appeared in newspapers ahead of a coordination meeting on Durga Puja preparations at Milan Mela Prangan.CPIM leader Shatarup Ghosh was among those who criticised the depiction.

Article Title: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari announces crackdown on child marriage after 60,000 underage deliveries
Article Text:
File photo: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari (Picture credit: PTI)

Nearly 60,000 underage deliveries reported in six months

Husbands, facilitators face legal action

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Government targets families and those facilitating marriages

NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday announced a statewide crackdown on child marriage, ordering house-to-house drives to identify underage marriages and pregnancies and warning of arrests, imprisonment and withdrawal of government welfare benefits for those involved.Speaking to the media at Nabanna after a Cabinet meeting, Adhikari said the government would invoke the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 and the POCSO Act against those marrying minors as well as people who facilitate or solemnise such marriages.The announcement came after the state health department reported nearly 60,000 institutional deliveries involving underage girls between January 1 and June 30, according to figures cited by the chief minister.Adhikari said Murshidabad recorded the highest number, with 12,847 institutional childbirths by underage girls during the six-month period. South 24 Parganas followed with 4,178 cases.He said West Bengal tops the country in child marriages and childbirths involving girls below 18 years of age.The chief minister said every case of pregnancy and childbirth involving a girl below 18 must be reported. The health records would be used by authorities to identify suspected child marriages and initiate action against those responsible.The proposed house-to-house drives will involve coordination between the police, health and social welfare departments and district administrations, with records of underage pregnancies and institutional deliveries being used to identify vulnerable cases.Adhikari said husbands of women found to have been married while underage would be issued showcause notices and asked to produce valid proof of their wife's age."If they fail to provide valid proof of the age, strict action will be taken," he said.He warned that police would initiate criminal action and make arrests in cases detected during the crackdown."Police action will be initiated, and arrests will be made," Adhikari said.The government will also withdraw welfare and other scheme benefits from people found to be involved in child marriages, he said.The chief minister issued a warning to priests, qazis and others who solemnise or facilitate underage marriages. Those found involved would face imprisonment and fines under the law.The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act provides for imprisonment of up to two years and/or a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh for people involved in promoting, permitting or conducting a child marriage.Adhikari also said the POCSO Act would be strictly applied, pointing out that sexual relations with a girl below 18 constitute an offence irrespective of whether she is married.He said physical relations with a girl below 18 attract provisions of the POCSO Act, with prison terms ranging from 10 years to life imprisonment and, in certain circumstances, the death penalty.Cases involving pregnancy of minors would attract particularly strict scrutiny and action, he said.The crackdown will target not only families arranging underage marriages but also husbands, facilitators and those conducting the ceremonies, with authorities expected to use health records to identify suspected cases.The issue has particular significance in West Bengal, where 19th-century social reformer Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar led campaigns against child marriage and for women's education.Adhikari also alleged that the previous Trinamool Congress government had failed to share data on child marriages and underage childbirths with the Centre.The chief minister said the administration would treat cases of child marriage as offences requiring police action and prosecution under the applicable laws.
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari announces statewide crackdown on child marriage. Nearly 60,000 institutional deliveries involving underage girls between January 1 and June 30. Murshidabad recorded the highest number, with 12,847 institutional childbirths by underage girls.

Article Title: West Bengal government bans liquor sales on Maha Ashtami, DJ music during Durga Puja
Article Text:
CM Suvendu Adhikari made the announcements at a coordination meeting at Milan Mela Prangan.

DJ music banned, themes to face scrutiny

Immersion deadline and special arrangements

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: West Bengal has announced a series of restrictions for this year’s Durga Puja, including a one-day ban on liquor sales, a complete prohibition on DJ music and curbs on the use of major roads for Puja-related activities.Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari made the announcements on Monday at a coordination meeting with Durga Puja committees at Milan Mela Prangan. The measures are aimed at ensuring that celebrations remain peaceful and orderly.All liquor shops and bars across the state will remain closed on Maha Ashtami, when devotees offer anjali to Goddess Durga."On the day when devotees offer anjali (Maha Ashtami) to Maa Durga, all liquor shops in the state will remain closed. There will be no liquor available in bars either," he said.The decision comes despite liquor traditionally seeing strong demand during the Puja period.The government will also prohibit DJ music during the celebrations and immersion processions.Adhikari asked Puja committees to ensure that their idols, pandals and themes do not offend religious sentiments or go against Sanatan traditions. Theme-based Pujas will still be allowed, but organisers have been asked to be more careful while choosing their concepts.The administration has also placed restrictions on roads being used for Puja activities. National highways cannot be blocked for organising Pujas, while 13 major roads in Kolkata, including Red Road and Cathedral Road, have been identified as areas where such activities will not be allowed.Puja inaugurations will also not be permitted before the start of Devi Paksha.Devi Paksha refers to the bright lunar fortnight in the Hindu month of Ashwin associated with the worship and invocation of Goddess Durga. The previous Trinamool Congress government under Mamata Banerjee had faced allegations over inaugurations being held before Devi Paksha began.Adhikari said organisers would have to complete idol immersions within the stipulated period before Lakshmi Puja."There will be no forcing or threatening anyone to change the immersion date," he said.The state has also planned cultural programmes in six major cities over two days, along with special events at six designated immersion ghats.Special arrangements will be made to help persons with disabilities, residents of old-age homes and people staying in ashrams visit Puja venues.The government will also set up an impartial jury for the Sharad Samman awards. Adhikari said the jury members would be chosen for their knowledge of the traditional, ritual and cultural aspects of Durga Puja. The Sharad Samman awards recognise Durga Puja organisers for creative and artistic excellence.The announcements come as West Bengal prepares for its first Durga Puja under the BJP government. The administration is seeking to manage the large-scale celebrations while imposing restrictions intended to maintain public order and protect religious and cultural sentiments.
Article Summary: All liquor shops and bars across the state will remain closed on Maha Ashtami, when devotees offer anjali to Goddess Durga. The government will also prohibit DJ music during the celebrations and immersion processions. Theme-based Pujas will still be allowed, but organisers have been asked to be more careful while choosing their concepts.

Satya Niketan PG building

collapsed during repair work

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha LoP and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday and the BJP government over the collapse of a PG building in Delhi’s Satya Niketan, accusing the government of failing to prevent such accidents and holding those responsible accountable.In a post on X, Gandhi accused that the BJP government follows a pattern of taking no preventive action before accidents and then “grandstanding” after tragedies, while blaming a few lower-level officials and allowing those he described as the “real culprits” to escape accountability.Gandhi said the Satya Niketan collapse was “no isolated tragedy” and referred to other recent incidents in Delhi, including deaths in Saidulajab and a fire in Hauz Rani. He alleged that lives and aspirations were repeatedly being lost in such incidents while meaningful action remained absent.“Every time, lives, dreams, and aspirations get buried under rubble, and every time, any real action is nowhere to be found,” Rahul said.The Congress leader also accused the Prime Minister of attempting to shame and silence those who question the government by using labels such as “dimagi naxal” and “naraz fufa”.He said the alleged lack of accountability was a consequence of a lack of political intent.“For 12 years, this government has spun you around with lofty talk about the whole world, but never addressed the real issues,” Gandhi said, questioning the BJP government's record on public safety.He also raised questions over governance in Delhi, saying the city has a “triple engine” government and asking what the excuse was for the administration's alleged helplessness in dealing with recurring safety failures.The building in Satya Niketan, near Delhi University's South Campus, housed a boys' paying-guest accommodation.It collapsed on Sunday while repair work was underway, leaving seven people dead and several others injured.The Delhi high court on Monday termed the Satya Niketan building collapse as "most unfortunate", and questioned not only the responsibility of the building owners but also that of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) and Delhi University (DU), which it said had failed to provide adequate accommodation for outstation students dependent on private paying guest (PG) facilities.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha LoP and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday.
