Article Title: 'Let me live the way I want to': Bengal BJP chief rejects Bageshwar Baba's meat diktat
Article Text:
Samik Bhattacharya said Bengalis would continue following their traditional food practices.

BJP leader backs Bengal’s food traditions

Shastri’s visit takes on political overtones

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BJP chief comments on Durga Puja advert

NEW DELHI: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya has rejected Dhirendra Shastri’s appeal to people in the state to avoid non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja, saying Bengal’s traditional food habits cannot be dictated by a visiting religious preacher.Shastri, popularly known as Bageshwar Baba, had urged people to give up non-vegetarian food during the festival and described those who continued eating it as "pakhandis" (heretics).Responding to the remarks, Bhattacharya said Bengalis would continue following their traditional food practices and stressed that an outsider could not decide what people in the state should eat or wear."Let me live the way I want to. Bengalis will eat what they have been eating. Can Bengalis not eat fish and meat? Swami Vivekananda has said it. Who is above him?" Bhattacharya said."Here, goat meat is offered as an offering to Maa Kali," he added.Bhattacharya said eating 'luchi' (puris) on Ashtami and goat meat on Navami has long been part of Bengali tradition during Durga Puja. He said there was no question of abandoning these practices because of Shastri’s appeal."We generally eat 'luchi' on Ashtami and goat meat on Navami.We will continue to do that. Nobody can tell the people of West Bengal what they should eat," he said.While saying that he respected Shastri as a religious figure, Bhattacharya argued that his personal views should not be treated as rules for Bengali society."A saint or a doctor may have the right to advise people to become vegetarian. But nobody coming from outside can sit in Bengal and decide who will eat what and who will wear what," he said.He also stressed that Shastri's remarks represented his personal views.The issue has sparked a wider debate in West Bengal, where fish and meat are closely associated with traditional Bengali food and religious practices vary across communities and regions. The practice of offering goat meat to Goddess Kali at several temples has also been cited in the debate.The controversy comes days after Shastri made his appeal during his visit to West Bengal. His visit has also attracted political attention after he was able to hold religious programmes across the state under the BJP government, despite allegations that he had faced difficulties in obtaining permission during the previous Trinamool Congress regime.Bhattacharya’s comments indicate that the BJP’s West Bengal unit does not support any attempt to impose a blanket vegetarian prescription on the state’s population during Durga Puja.The BJP has been trying to expand its presence in West Bengal by combining its Hindutva politics with an appeal to Bengali cultural identity. Shastri’s remarks have highlighted the challenge of balancing religious messaging with the state’s distinct food and cultural traditions.Bhattacharya also commented on a separate controversy involving a West Bengal government advertisement that showed Goddess Durga with 11 hands.He advised against turning what he described as a "possible technical or printing error by the advertising agency" into a political issue and said the mistake should simply be corrected.The BJP leader’s response to both controversies reflects an attempt by the state unit to distinguish religious beliefs from Bengal’s established cultural practices, particularly when it comes to food during Durga Puja.
Article Summary: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya rejects Dhirendra Shastri’s appeal to people in the state to avoid non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja. He said Bengalis would continue following their traditional food practices and stressed that an outsider could not decide what people should eat.

Article Title: Far-right AfD makes historic breakthrough in Germany, wins 44% in state poll
Article Text:
Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is poised for a historic breakthrough in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.

Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is poised for a historic breakthrough in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, opening the prospect of the party seeking to govern despite falling short of an outright majority.With most interim results counted, the AfD was projected to secure a record 44% of the vote and far ahead of the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), which stood at 17%.Ulrich Siegmund, the AfD’s prominent leader in Saxony-Anhalt, described the result as “sensational” and said the party wanted to begin governing as soon as possible.According to the BBC report, a victory would mark an unprecedented development in post-war Germany, where no far-right party has previously taken control of a state government. State-level power would give the AfD influence over areas including policing, education and culture.Saxony-Anhalt, home to about 2.1 million people, has been a particular focus of concern because the state’s AfD branch is classified as “right-wing extremist” by Germany’s domestic intelligence service. Siegmund, 35, rejects the designation.Siegmund and the party’s national co-leaders, Alice Weidel and Tino Chrupalla, celebrated as exit polls showed the AfD was on course to more than double its 2021 vote share.The AfD’s strong performance was quickly described by political opponents and commentators as a major turning point, highlighting the growing influence of the far-right party in German politics. Public broadcaster Das Erste even replaced its long-running crime drama Tatort with special coverage examining the significance of the result.“This isn’t just about Saxony-Anhalt,” Siegmund told supporters. “It’s a signal for the whole of Germany - a self-confident signal.”Commentators and political opponents spoke of the outcome as a watershed and break with the past. Main TV channel Das Erste cancelled its legendary crime drama Tatort to focus on what the result meant.“This result is not just about Saxony-Anhalt,” Siegmund told supporters, calling it “a signal for the whole of Germany — a confident signal.”The result also drew attention abroad. US President Donald Trump shared a screenshot of the German election projection on his Truth Social platform, which Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev later reposted, describing the outcome as a “historic win for the pragmatic AfD”.Dmitriev had previously praised the Russia-friendly party as one offering “hope and reason” and greater cooperation for Germany. US Vice-President JD Vance also backed the AfD ahead of Germany’s federal election last year, a move that drew criticism in Germany over alleged foreign political interference.Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, however, offered a sharply contrasting reaction. The centre-right leader said that in Poland, “only idiots and traitors can rejoice at the triumph of the AfD.”Despite its strong performance, the AfD lacks the seats needed to govern alone, leaving Ulrich Siegmund facing a difficult path to power. He has so far ruled out leading a minority government, even as the party’s national leadership considers that option possible.Siegmund said the AfD would instead be willing to seek support from individual lawmakers or another party. “If necessary there’ll just be new elections, then we’d just get 50 or 55%,” he said.The outcome was also closely tied to the performance of the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW), whose ability to clear the 5% threshold needed to enter the state parliament remained uncertain for several hours. Interim results eventually showed the party had crossed the threshold, meaning the AfD would not gain the additional seats it might otherwise have secured.The AfD was projected to win 39 of the 83 seats in Saxony-Anhalt’s state parliament, leaving it three seats short of the 42 required for an outright majority.
Article Summary: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is poised for a historic breakthrough in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. The AfD was projected to secure a record 44% of the vote and far ahead of the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), which stood at 17%. Ulrich Siegmund, the AfD’s prominent leader in Saxony, described the result as ‘sensational’

Article Title: Eiffel Tower shuts after female staff allegedly sidelined during Hindu group's visit
Article Text:
Also Read:

NEW DELHI: The Eiffel Tower was closed to visitors on Monday after staff staged a walkout over allegations that female employees were moved away from their workstations during a visit by a Hindu religious group linked to the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS), as reported by Euronews.The iconic Paris landmark's operator, SETE, said the closure was due to "exceptional circumstances".The protest followed a visit by around 100 people linked to the BAPS Hindu movement, which inaugurated a new temple in France over the weekend.Diane Davoine, a union representative, told French TV that female workers had been "moved away from their workstations as the delegation passed by" during the group's visit on Saturday.Eiffel Tower employees condemned what they described as "professional instructions that led to female employees being sidelined, replaced and made invisible because of their sex."SETE acknowledged that the Hindu delegation had requested that the visit be organised to limit "interactions with women", but said "these conditions should not have been accepted."In a statement on Monday evening, the BAPS Hindu temple in Paris said it took the concerns "very seriously" and apologised for "any pain or inconvenience caused.""Due to the size of our delegation, the visit was arranged in conjunction with the Eiffel Tower team at the start of normal opening hours to avoid disrupting or inconveniencing others," it said."To the best of our knowledge, at no point was anyone prevented access to the Eiffel Tower," it continued, adding that it believed in the "universal values of mutual respect and service."Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire said on X that he was "aware of the outcry among the employees of the Eiffel Tower" and called it "unacceptable" that such conditions were agreed to."These are not my values, nor are they the values that the Eiffel Tower should uphold, where everyone must be able to move about and act freely, without distinction between women and men," he wrote, adding that an investigation into the incident would be launched.National assembly president Yael Braun-Pivet also condemned the incident."I refuse to accept that women should be told to step aside to meet the demands of foreign visitors," she said. "Welcoming others never means giving up our values. In France, women are fully present in public life. No one tells them to become invisible there."The incident comes day after the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) inaugurated its first major Hindu temple in France, marking a significant moment for the Hindu community in the country.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday hailed India-France ties while addressing the inauguration of the Swaminarayan temple in Paris. He said the strategic partnership between the two countries was particularly special as it was built on a foundation of long-standing cultural and political ties.The PM said he hoped the grand temple would stand for centuries as a symbol of cooperation and opportunity between India and France.“In recent years, relations between India and France have reached new heights. Together with my friend, President (Emmanuel) Macron, both nations are building a Special Global Strategic Partnership,” he said.
Article Summary: The iconic Paris landmark's operator, SETE, said the closure was due to "exceptional circumstances" The protest followed a visit by around 100 people linked to the BAPS Hindu movement. A union representative said female workers had been "moved away from their workstations as the delegation passed by"

Article Title: Gifted Manipuri guitarist who built his life around music in Delhi for 20 years beaten to death outside home
Article Text:
Chongtham Vikram Singh, a gifted guitarist, died after being beaten outside his home.





NEW DELHI/KOLKATA: Chongtham Vikram Singh was a gifted guitarist who had spent years turning music into his language, playing lead guitar for bands in Manipur before moving to Delhi nearly 20 years ago and building a life around his passion. On Sunday night, his music fell silent after he was allegedly beaten mercilessly by eight people outside his home. He died during treatment around 6.30am Monday.The men were allegedly intoxicated and creating a ruckus outside the house around 11pm. According to Singh's family, he went downstairs to stop them. A few minutes later, Singh (55) was heard banging on the door and screaming, "Thong hango! Thong hango! (open the door, open the door)."His son, 20-year-old Yaiphaba, found Singh in a semi-conscious state, with his T-shirt ripped apart. He was rushed to Holy Family Hospital, where doctors found that his blood pressure had fallen below 50mm Hg. His condition was too critical for surgery and he died Monday morning.A resident of Thangmeiband Lourung Purel Leikai in Imphal West, Singh opened a music school in Delhi, mentored students at home and also taught at Delhi School of Music.His musical journey took him to the Rock'n'Roots project, where he collaborated with Rajasthani folk singer Mame Khan. He also collaborated with other renowned musicians for cultural shows and concerts.Singh, a cousin of Lakshmipriya Devi, the director of India's first BAFTA Award-winning film, Boong, is survived by his wife Jyotsana (54) and son Yaiphaba. While Jyotsana works as a senior consultant with an MNC, Yaiphaba is a law student. Singh's mother, 86-year-old Chongtham Ongbi Kamala Devi, is a renowned classical and modern Manipuri singer.Talking to TOI from Imphal, Singh's brother, Vivek, said, "We haven't told our father, Dr Chongtham Birendra Singh, who is 96, about it, fearing that he might not be able to bear the loss. My mother is unconsolable."Friends remembered Singh as a gentle and accomplished musician who was passionate about his craft.Manipuri associations in Delhi said though the postmortem was over, they didn't want the body to be sent back to Manipur till justice was done. "Once the last rites are over, only the family bears the loss, and the incident fades into oblivion," a Manipuri activist in Delhi said. Northeast student groups, friends and family members staged a protest outside Sunlight Colony police station.
Article Summary: Chongtham Vikram Singh, a gifted guitarist, died after being beaten outside his home. The men were allegedly intoxicated and creating a ruckus outside the house. According to Singh's family, he went downstairs to stop them. His condition was too critical for surgery and he died Monday morning.

Article Title: ‘Russia ready to negotiate’: Zelenskyy after meeting US envoys Witkoff and Kushner
Article Text:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy

(With AP inputs)

Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday (local time) said US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff told him that Russia is “ready to negotiate” when they met him in Kyiv after meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.“Russia really thinks that this winter can help them break us. But the Trump administration could pressure Putin to de-escalate... Putin doesn’t want to upset President Trump,” Zelenskyy told US news outlet Axios.“The US envoys told me that the Russians are ready to negotiate,” he added.Elaborating on his discussions with Witkoff and Kushner, the Ukrainian leader noted that the weekend talks included US proposals concerning energy facilities, grain shipments, and oil and gas exports, but declined to provide further details.“The US is seeking to restart negotiations between Ukraine and Russia and wants to ensure the coming winter is different from previous ones. The aim is to make progress before or during winter to ‘bring (the) sides closer to peace,’” Zelenskyy said.Russia has targeted Ukraine’s energy infrastructure every winter since the war began in February 2022, leaving millions without electricity and heating as temperatures have fallen as low as -20°C.The visits to Moscow and Kyiv by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner mark Washington’s latest effort to break the diplomatic deadlock in Europe’s deadliest conflict since World War II.US President Donald Trump had repeatedly claimed during his campaign that, if elected, he would end the Russia-Ukraine conflict “in 24 hours.” Last August, more than six months into his second and final term, Trump hosted Putin in Alaska to discuss the conflict, marking their first meeting since Trump returned to office. However, the meeting ended without any significant breakthrough.
Article Summary: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff told him that Russia is ‘ready to negotiate’ The Ukrainian leader noted that the weekend talks included US proposals concerning energy facilities, grain shipments, and oil and gas exports.

Article Title: Yemen conflict widens: Houthis claim strikes on Saudi airport, air base and Aramco sites
Article Text:
Drones and ballistic missiles at King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait and Abha International Airport in southern Saudi Arabia. (GIF: @theinformant_x)

Houthi attacks follow September 7 escalation

Houthi official puts prison toll at 11

Fighting intensifies near Bab al-Mandab

Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis said on September 8 that they had launched missiles and drones at Abha International Airport, King Khalid air base and Aramco facilities in Abha and Jizan.“Yemeni drones and missiles pound the Saudi enemy,” Houthi media outlet Ansarollah said on Telegram. Another Ansarollah post named the airport, military base and oil facilities among the targets.The Saudi-led coalition said on September 7 that 73 people were injured in Houthi attacks on civilian and economic sites. The attacks affected Abha, Khamis Mushait, Najran and Jazan, and the coalition said it would respond firmly, according to Reuters.On the same day, the Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of air strikes and cruise missile attacks in Jawf, Al-Bayda, Marib and Taiz. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the alleged Saudi attacks “will not go unanswered or unpunished”. Saudi Arabia did not publicly confirm the Houthi allegations.One of the alleged Saudi strikes hit a prison in Al-Hazm, Jawf province, according to Houthi media. The Houthi-run health ministry initially reported seven deaths, including a child, and at least seven injuries, according to the Associated Press.Separately, Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces said their own warplanes struck Houthi positions on September 7.By September 8, Jawf civil defence chief Hassan Saboula put the Houthi-reported prison death toll at 11 and said 20 inmates remained missing beneath the rubble, according to the Houthi-run Al-Masirah. Houthi-affiliated Saba said a child visiting the facility was among those killed.The latest exchange comes amid fighting near Yemen’s Red Sea coast. More than 300 people have been killed in the recent clashes, while hundreds of families have been forced from their homes. The Houthis are pressing an offensive for territory along the Bab al-Mandab Strait.Bab al-Mandab connects the Gulf of Aden with the Red Sea, which leads north to the Suez Canal. The route has gained importance for Saudi crude shipments as Iran’s blockade restricts traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.
Article Summary: Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis said on September 8 that they had launched missiles and drones at Abha International Airport, King Khalid air base and Aramco facilities in Abha and Jizan. On the same day, the Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of air strikes and cruise missile attacks in Jawf, Al-Bayda, Marib and Taiz. Saudi Arabia did not publicly confirm the Houthi allegations.

Article Title: PLA report warns Chinese cities of potential nuclear attacks, flags Japan as ‘threat’
Article Text:
AI-generated image

Why report singled out Japan

What a potential nuclear attack on a Chinese city look like

A new study by China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Rocket Force has warned Chinese cities to prepare for potential nuclear attacks, singling out Japan as a “major danger signal” to the world.According to the report, the likelihood of a large-scale global nuclear war was “relatively low,” South China Morning Post reported.“However, the possibility cannot be ruled out that small or medium-sized nuclear-armed or potentially nuclear-armed states, driven by geopolitical or religious conflicts, could carry out a single nuclear-weapon terrorist attack on neighbouring countries or on key cities of major powers,” it said.The study noted that Tokyo had yet to join the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, the first legally binding international agreement banning nuclear arms, adopted in 2017. It also claimed Japan was considering changes to its long-standing “three non-nuclear principles” of not possessing, producing or permitting the introduction of nuclear weapons.“Japan has still not acceded to the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, and the current Japanese government is even openly considering revising the principle of ‘non-introduction of nuclear weapons’ within its ‘three non-nuclear principles’, sending a major danger signal to the international community,” the report stated.In January 2022, the United Nations P5 — China, the United States, Russia, Britain, and France — the five permanent members of the UN Security Council — issued a joint statement affirming that “a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought”.But the PLA study warned: “Once certain countries or terrorist groups take such a risk, the possibility that Chinese cities could suffer a nuclear terrorist attack cannot be ruled out.”An official Chinese report released in January alleged that Tokyo “may already have produced weapons-grade plutonium in secret” and possessed “the technological and economic capabilities to achieve nuclear armament in a short period of time.”The January report also claimed Japan had “established a comprehensive nuclear fuel cycle system and possesses robust nuclear industrial capabilities”.The PLA Rocket Force study also modelled a scenario in which a major Chinese city was hit by a single, low-yield nuclear terrorist attack involving a tactical weapon.Drawing on historical data from the 1945 Hiroshima bombing in Japan, along with simulations conducted worldwide, the researchers identified a range of challenges for medical teams, including hazardous conditions, widespread social disorder and complex patterns of injuries.Beijing has already established an emergency rescue network with more than 30 bases to treat casualties from a nuclear attack. The researchers called for further expansion of treatment capacity, additional resources and specialised training.They also recommended that local authorities stockpile emergency supplies, including antibiotics and radiation-protection equipment, and keep them in a state of “combat readiness”.Public education should also be strengthened on nuclear and radiation safety, rescue protocols and protective measures to minimise panic and irrational behaviour during an emergency.Compared with the medical response to an accident at a civilian nuclear facility, even a low-yield nuclear terrorist attack could result in heavy casualties and complex, multi-trauma injuries.Such an event would pose a “huge test” for the medical capacity of any city or country, the authors wrote, urging China to “prepare for a rainy day”.Beijing has repeatedly accused Tokyo of pursuing “remilitarisation” and has long voiced suspicions about its nuclear ambitions.
Article Summary: China's People's Liberation Army Rocket Force warns Chinese cities to prepare for potential nuclear attacks. Study singles out Japan as a ‘major danger signal’ to the world. Tokyo has yet to join the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons.

Article Title: 'Strike our assets & you get struck': Iran threatens US energy assets in Gulf after latest clashes
Article Text:
Iran threatens US oil, gas assets.

Iran tightens restrictions

Oil flows disrupted

Iran has threatened to retaliate against any new US attacks on its assets, warning that American oil and gas interests and energy infrastructure across the Gulf could be targeted as tensions escalate over the Strait of Hormuz."Strike our assets and you get struck," Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said after US and Iranian forces traded strikes on shipping over the weekend, pushing oil prices to near six-week highs on Monday, according to Reuters.The warning came amid growing concerns that the conflict could escalate further, with diplomatic efforts showing little progress towards restoring normal energy flows through the Gulf.Iran has tightened restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and gas supplies, since the war began with US and Israeli strikes on February 28.On Sunday, senior Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran would soon announce a new restricted zone in the Gulf and establish a new shipping corridor through the strait.Rezaei said the restricted zone would begin where a US naval blockade of Iran starts and extend into parts of the Gulf.Ships entering the area would be placed on an Iranian sanctions list."We will only commit to the Strait of Hormuz being open when they (the Americans) stop the sabotage, threats and attacks on Iran," Rezaei said.Qalibaf later reinforced the warning in an apparent response to US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who had described Iran's oil tanker fleet as "defenceless"."It's simple: the oil and gas production chain here is sprawling, accessible, and exposed. American oil and gas companies across these waters and facilities share that exposure," Qalibaf, who is Iran's top negotiator, wrote on X.Tensions have intensified after a relative lull through much of August and the collapse of an interim ceasefire reached in June.Earlier on Saturday, US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers, including one near Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export hub, according to US Central Command. The strikes followed attacks by Iran's Revolutionary Guards on US warships operating in the region.Shipping data showed that an average of only 10 commodity vessels a day passed through the Strait of Hormuz over the past 10 days, the lowest level since May. The strait is a critical energy chokepoint. Before the war, it carried about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments.Regional tensions were also heightened by Israeli strikes on a town in southern Lebanon that killed at least 12 people on Monday, according to Lebanon's health ministry.The strikes have raised fears of a renewed Israeli military campaign despite a June ceasefire with Iran-backed Hezbollah. Tehran has insisted that any lasting agreement with Washington must include an end to Israeli attacks in Lebanon.Iran has said it will step up efforts to address problems caused by US sanctions, which have put further pressure on its economy.Three senior Iranian sources told Reuters that Washington's campaign to restrict Iranian oil exports and curb sanctions evasion is becoming increasingly difficult for Tehran to withstand.Qalibaf acknowledged over the weekend that Iran's challenges extend beyond the battlefield. Alongside the military conflict, he cited inflation, unemployment, currency volatility and market instability as major domestic problems.The conflict has also affected Gulf oil producers, including the United Arab Emirates, which has faced Iranian missile attacks and attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.The disruption is also being felt in the United States, where higher fuel prices have added to economic pressures and could weigh on President Donald Trump's popularity ahead of November's midterm elections.
Article Summary: Iran has threatened to retaliate against any new US attacks on its assets. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said American oil and gas interests and energy infrastructure could be targeted. The warning came amid growing concerns that the conflict could escalate further.

Article Title: Indonesia air travel resumes after two-day disruption from volcanic ash
Article Text:
Air travel across Indonesia’s capital region began returning to normal early Tuesday.

Air travel across Indonesia’s capital region began returning to normal early Tuesday following a two-day shutdown triggered by volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau, which disrupted nearly 3,000 flights.Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and Halim Perdanakusuma Airport in Jakarta, along with Husein Sastranegara Airport in West Java’s Bandung and two smaller airports in Banten province, reopened shortly after midnight, Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said.Three other airports, including Radin Inten II Airport in Lampung at the southern end of Sumatra, remained closed until 10 a.m. despite improving conditions. Atung Bungsu Airport in Pagar Alam, South Sumatra, resumed normal operations on Monday morning.“We are taking a cautious approach because wind direction can change rapidly,” Purwagandhi said in a statement. “We want to make sure volcanic ash has moved away from airports around Anak Krakatau.”While tests at several airports found no traces of volcanic ash, the prolonged closures would provide additional time to inspect and clean runways, taxiways, aircraft and other equipment that may have been exposed to the ash, Purwagandhi said.The continuous eruption at Anak Krakatau, marked by lava fountains and loud explosions, subsided on Sunday, but the volcanic island remained active on Tuesday morning. Eruptions were recorded at 5:08 a.m. and 5:34 a.m., although the height of the ash column could not be determined.A massive two-day air travel disruption affected approximately 341,000 passengers as airport closures on Sunday and Monday grounded nearly 2,961 flights—including 622 international routes—according to reports by the Associated Press.The government also allowed schools in areas affected by volcanic ash to temporarily switch to online classes to limit students’ exposure to the ash.Anak Krakatau is a volcanic island in the Sunda Strait, located between Indonesia’s main islands of Java and Sumatra. Its name means “child of Krakatau” and refers to the volcano that emerged from the remnants of the infamous Krakatau, whose massive 1883 eruption triggered a period of global cooling.In 2018, an eruption of Anak Krakatau generated a tsunami that killed at least 430 people across Sumatra and Java. Researchers believe the volcanic activity triggered an underwater landslide, causing part of the volcano’s southwestern slope to collapse and displace a large volume of seawater.The volcano has remained at Indonesia’s second-highest alert level since July, with authorities urging residents, tourists and fishermen to stay at least 3 kilometres (1.9 miles) away from the active crater.
Article Summary: Air travel across Indonesia’s capital region began returning to normal early Tuesday following a two-day shutdown triggered by volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau. Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and Halim Perdanakusuma Airport in Jakarta reopened shortly after midnight. Three other airports, including Radin Inten II Airport in Lampung at the southern end of Sumatra, remained closed until 10 a.m.

Article Title: EU debate takes shape as Macron backs under-15 social media ban
Article Text:
French President Emmanuel Macron (Photo: AP)

Macron seeks one age limit across EU

Court blocked French ban before September rollout

High school phone restrictions take effect

France is preparing a second attempt at restricting social media for children under 15 while President Emmanuel Macron presses Brussels to turn the same age limit into a common European rule.He made the EU push in an August 29 letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, calling for a new "European legislative text" to "protect all children in the Union". The request came after France's Constitutional Council stopped the country's planned restrictions before they could take effect on September 1.In his letter, Macron told von der Leyen that it was now "essential to go further" and harmonise the under-15 restriction through European legislation. He has also sought support among EU countries for a common "digital majority", although governments differ over the age at which unrestricted social media access should begin, AFP reported. Von der Leyen has said Europe should consider "phased and gradual access for different age ranges".Recommendations presented to the Commission would impose the tightest controls on children under 13 and allow broader access as they get older, provided platforms meet safety requirements.Nearly two-thirds of respondents to a recent EU survey backed age-based restrictions on children's social media access, according to the European Commission.France's parliament had backed restrictions barring children under 15 from social media from September 1. The Constitutional Council struck down the relevant provisions on August 14, meaning the ban never came into force.The proposed rules would also have required age verification and the closure of existing accounts belonging to users below the threshold. The council found the blanket restriction disproportionate, saying it did not sufficiently distinguish between platforms according to the risks they posed or between children based on factors including age, maturity and family circumstances. It also raised concerns over safeguards governing age verification and personal data, Reuters reported.The ruling nevertheless left room for another attempt. The council recognised protecting children's best interests as a legitimate constitutional objective, and Macron has said he hopes to "find a way forward" through a narrower measure that complies with both EU law and the French Constitution.His August 29 letter followed that ruling, taking the campaign to the European level even as France began work on a revised national text.A separate French measure restricting mobile phone use in schools did take effect with the start of the 2026-27 academic year. Rules already applied in primary and middle schools were extended to high schools from September 1, according to the French education ministry.While visiting Lycée Chaptal in Mende that day, Macron defended the measure, telling pupils that using a phone at school was "not compatible with paying attention in classes". He said the problem extended to adults, adding that attendees at some Elysée meetings were now asked to surrender their phones to prevent them from checking the devices during discussions.The school collected pupils' phones in numbered compartments during the visit. Reactions were mixed, with some students accepting the restriction and others describing it as "infantilising". Teachers' unions have questioned how rapidly schools can put the rules into practice.He also used the visit to return to social media access for minors. "This creates addictions and dependencies. It also leads to attention disorders," Macron told pupils. He added that heavier exposure to screens and social networks made it harder to sustain attention and concentrate on reading.France is now expected to produce revised national legislation in the coming months, while the European Commission prepares its own proposals following the expert panel's recommendations.
Article Summary: Macron writes to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. He calls for a new "European legislative text" to "protect all children in the Union" France's Constitutional Council stopped the country's planned restrictions on September 1. A separate French measure restricting mobile phone use in schools did take effect.

Article Title: Night entry, lifting clothes don't amount to rape bid: Jharkhand HC
Article Text:
Jharkhand high court





RANCHI: Entering a woman's house at night and trying to lift her clothes may be criminal, but it does not amount to an attempt to rape, Jharkhand HC has ruled while drawing a line between outraging a woman's modesty and attempting to rape her.Justice Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, deciding a criminal appeal on Aug 31, held that acts attributed to the appellant did not cross that legal threshold. HC upheld his conviction for using criminal force against a woman with the intention of outraging her modesty, finding evidence sufficient for the lesser offence. The judgement was released Monday.The court modified a July 25 sessions court order from East Singhbhum district that had sentenced the man to four years of rigorous imprisonment for attempted rape. It reduced his sentence to the nearly eight months he had already spent in custody, saying that was sufficient to meet the ends of justice. The appeal was partly allowed.The case dates to the night of Dec 26, 1999. The man was arrested on Dec 27 and later a chargesheet was filed alleging attempted rape.The trial court convicted him of attempted rape and handed him a four-year prison term. The appellant approached the high court.Justice Srivastava said an act can amount to attempted rape only when it is sufficiently proximate to the commission of rape. The evidence in this case did not make the leap from criminal force intended to outrage a woman's modesty to an attempt to rape, HC ruled.
Article Summary: Jharkhand high court rules that entering a woman's house at night does not amount to an attempt to rape. Court rules that acts attributed to the appellant did not cross that legal threshold. The case dates to the night of Dec 26, 1999. The trial court convicted him of attempted rape.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay spits fire at three generations of DMK leaders
Article Text:
Vijay started his speech around 9.33am, listing out measures taken by his govt to maintain law and order and ensure corruption-free governance.





CHENNAI: In his fiercest attack yet on DMK , Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay brought up the half-century-old Sarkaria Commission report and a 2025 Enforcement Directorate letter in the assembly on Monday, projecting three generations — M Karunanidhi, M K Stalin and Udhayanidhi Stalin — besides former Union minister Murasoli Maran as corrupt leaders.“Wherever DMK is present, there would be corruption. Wherever there is corruption, DMK will be present,’’ said Vijay in his response to the demand for grants for home department. His charges triggered loud protests from DMK members who stormed the well of the House after speaker J C D Prabhakar denied opposition leader Udhayanidhi permission to respond. DMK MLAs later walked out.Vijay started his speech around 9.33am, listing out measures taken by his govt to maintain law and order and ensure corruption-free governance. The situation turned chaotic in 20 minutes when Vijay sharpened his attack on the previous DMK govt.Citing the 1976 Sarkaria Commission report, Vijay said there was an entire chapter dedicated to ‘Veeranam pipeline scam’ and mentioned the alleged corruption by Karunanidhi and Maran.“The report says they demanded 2.5% commission for the project,’’ Vijay said. He then turned to the more recent DMK regime. Reading out from a letter sent by Enforcement Directorate in Dec 2025, he said Stalin and Udhayanidhi were direct beneficiaries of party fund.“They dared me to open the three files on my table. Before opening them, let me show a sample,” he said, reading out portions of the ED and DVAC reports.He alleged that there was corruption under former ministers K N Nehru and V Senthilbalaji. “They wanted proof of corruption. Here it is,’’ Vijay said, displaying a copy of the ED letter. Targeting Udhayanidhi, Vijay asked “who is Ratheesh” and why was he “hiding” in Dubai ever since TVK came to power.The CM said many DMK leaders used offensive language. He invoked former AIADMK CMs M G Ramachandran and J Jayalalithaa more than once to attack DMK. He also referred to Telugu Desam Party founder N T Rama Rao and positioned himself in the league of former chief ministers C N Annadurai, M G Ramachandran and N T Rama Rao. “Anna in 1967, MGR in 1977, NTR in 1983 and Vijay in 2026,’’ he said.Protesting the CM’s remarks, Udhayanidhi and other DMK MLAs stood up. Udhayanidhi sought permission to respond to the charges levelled against him as Vijay continued with his speech. DMK MLAs displayed pamphlets related to alleged corruption and crimes involving TVK functionaries, and repeatedly demanded that the speaker allow Udhayanidhi to speak. With no response from the Speaker, DMK MLAs entered the well of the House. The Speaker questioned the MLAs for bringing posters and pamphlets into the House without his permission.“The intention of DMK members is to prevent the CM from delivering his reply,’’ the speaker said, adding that he would not bend to pressure from the opposition. After some time, however, he said the CM had suggested that he allow the opposition leader to speak, and that he would consider the request. On hearing this, DMK legislators returned to their seats. However, the speaker refused to allow Udhayanidhi to speak, prompting the DMK members to walkout in protest.Later, Vijay helped DMK MLA Durai Chandrasekar, who was in the well of the House, get up.
Article Summary: Vijay started his speech around 9.33am, listing out measures taken by his govt to maintain law and order and ensure corruption-free governance. His charges triggered loud protests from DMK members who stormed the well of the House after speaker J C D Prabhakar denied opposition leader Udhayanidhi permission to respond.

Article Title: Satya Niketan building collapse: 2 more bodies found, toll climbs to 7; owner earned Rs 4L/month
Article Text:
The rescue and search operation has concluded while a small part of the debris is yet to be cleared.

PG netted owner Rs 4L/month





NEW DELHI: Delhi Police Monday arrested Hariram Gupta (81), who was operating the five-storey PG accommodation that collapsed in south Delhi's Satya Niketan on Sunday, from Bhiwadi in Rajasthan. He is a retired IAF sergeant. Gupta's wife Urmila (75) and their son Mahesh (52) have also been arrested.The toll in Sunday's incident rose to seven after two more bodies were extricated from the rubble early Monday. The deceased students have been identified as Arpit Jaj (19), Abhishek (20), Yuvraj Soni (20), Pawan (17) and Akshat Singh Yadav (18). Two labourers - Surinder Singh (56) and Param Lal Kori (30) - also died in the incident. The rescue and search operation has concluded while a small part of the debris is yet to be cleared.MCD has suspended five south zone officials - deputy commissioner Rakesh Kumar, superintending engineer Ranvir Singh, executive engineer (building) Lalit Kumar Goel, assistant engineer (building) Sunil Chauhan and junior engineer (building) Ashish Kumar.In a post on X, CM Rekha Gupta said: "The building owner has been arrested.Immediate sealing of buildings with unauthorised fifth floors has been ordered across Delhi. Nearby PGs and buildings are also being thoroughly inspected. Strict action, including sealing, will be taken against violations. Delhi govt has taken the matter with utmost seriousness. Anyone found guilty or responsible will not be spared." A formal order to seal buildings has, however, not been passed by MCD so far.The probe revealed that construction work had been under way at the property for the past two weeks. Sources said the work included plans to merge two shops, besides carrying out work to address waterlogging. The PG had only one entry and exit point. Investigators have also learned that multiple PG accommodations were being operated in the area under the same name, and are verifying whether they were connected to the same operator."The building was around 40-50 years old and additional floors were added from time to time. There was also commercial space on the premises. The current PG had been operating there for around a year," sources said. Searches are being conducted to trace the PG warden/manager and the labour contractor associated with the building. Their roles in the incident are also being examined.Delhi Police, meanwhile, said Hariram was apprehended after raids by over 10 teams were launched to net him. After he was found missing from his Gurgaon home, police used technical surveillance to trace his movements and opened a look-out circular against him to prevent him from leaving the country.A watch was also kept on the premises, including shops, owned by him and his family. The operation was monitored by joint commissioner Nupur Prasad. "Finding himself cornered, Hariram sent some messages seeking help, which alerted us to his location," said a senior cop.Police said five people are being treated for injuries. They have been identified as Asgar Ali (30), Neeraj Bawa (19), Aditya Kumar (19), Nitish Chib (19) and Md Ayan (18). They are undergoing treatment, with two of them reported to be in critical condition.During the investigation, police found the property is registered in the name of Gupta's wife Urmila, but was managed and operated by her husband. Electricity connections for two floors of the building are also registered in his name. Their son, Mahesh, runs a hardware and paint shop.A special team has been formed to investigate the case and officers have sought the ownership documents of the building as well as its map and other permissions.Initial probe and interview with students has revealed around 15 cramped rooms had been carved out in the 55-square-yard house to house 45 students. Three students were lodged in each room and every occupant was charged at least Rs 10,000 per month. The property, sources said, is believed to be generating a revenue of over Rs 4 lakh per month.The probe, sources said, will also extend to "PG mafia" in the area - private players facilitating illegal construction and operation of PGs on commission basis.A purported rent agreement for the PG has also surfaced. It purportedly states: "In case of any personal injury suffered/loss/damage of personal belongings of the tenant due to reasons beyond the control of the PG vize sealing/fire/earthquake/heavy rains/other natural calamities etc, the hostel will not be liable for paying any compensation."The document adds: "PG authorities are not responsible for any casualties to tenants."
Article Summary: Hariram Gupta (81), who was operating the five-storey PG accommodation, arrested. Gupta's wife Urmila (75) and their son Mahesh (52) have also been arrested. The toll in Sunday's incident rose to seven after two more bodies were extricated from the rubble early Monday.

Article Title: Injured govindas advised CT scans, Shiv Sena men assault Palghar hospital staffer
Article Text:
The Sainiks also entered the ICU & general ward, removed IV lines & took away the 5 injured govindas

By- Suhas.Birhade





PALGHAR: Some Shiv Sena workers allegedly assaulted an employee of a private hospital in Palghar, abused doctors and threatened to damage property early on Sunday after being told that five govindas injured during a dahi handi celebration needed to undergo CT scans.Sena’s district chief Kundan Sankhe claimed they went to Relief Hospital after receiving complaints that the govindas were not being allowed to leave and were being asked to settle the bill, which was to be covered by the party. He said a dispute arose after hospital staffers failed to give satisfactory answers.Palghar police filed a case under various sections against 17 persons, including Rohit Gavit, son of Sena MLA Rajendra Gavit and the party’s deputy taluka chief, Sankhe, and the city Sena chief. The assault was captured on a CCTV camera in the hospital’s reception. Kishor Manbhav, senior inspector, said police examined the CCTV footage and launched a search for the accused.The assault came two months after Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre and his aides allegedly assaulted medical staffers of a Dombivli hospital purportedly over delay in treating a pregnant patient.Around 1.15am on Sunday, Sena’s district chief Kundan Sankhe, its city chief Rahul Gharat and other workers allegedly entered Relief Hospital in Palghar, questioning doctors over the treatment and the need for the injured govindas to undergo CT scans.A woman doctor working near the reception reportedly explained that the scans were necessary because the patients had suffered head injuries.The Sena workers allegedly became angry, threatened to damage hospital property and abused doctors. Gharat then allegedly slapped the receptionist, Vivek Zinga (23). The assault was caught on camera.The workers then allegedly entered the ICU, removed the intravenous fluid lines of govindas, and took all five of them away from the hospital.Sena had organised a dahi handi celebration on Saturday, during which the five govindas were injured. Three were in the ICU with head injuries and two in the general ward. Their bill had reached Rs 19,866, of which a Sena worker had paid Rs 10,000, with the remaining amount reportedly to be paid by the party’s district chief.The hospital administration said Sankhe questioned why the patients had been admitted to the ICU and why the bill was so high, and intimidated and assaulted the staff. “Our entire staff is frightened. The employee who was assaulted is under stress. Strict action should be taken against all those who assaulted him,” said the hospital’s Dr Vishal Kotgirkar.Sections 115(2) (causing hurt), 351(2) and 352 (insulting and threatening with the intention of causing a breach of peace), 329(4) (criminal trespass), and 189(1), 189(2) and 190 (unlawful assembly), as well as Sections 3 and 4 of Maharashtra Medicare Service Persons and Medicare Service Institutions Act, 2010, relating to assault on medical personnel, violent acts and damage to hospital property, have been invoked in the case.The Boisar unit of Indian Medical Association, represented by president Dr Milan Kamat and secretary Dr Prakash Babu, expressed concern over the attack and sought appropriate preventive measures to ensure the safety and security of the hospital and its staffers.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena workers allegedly assaulted an employee of a private hospital in Palghar, abused doctors and threatened to damage property. The workers entered the ICU, removed the intravenous fluid lines of govindas, and took all five of them away from the hospital. The assault was captured on a CCTV camera in the hospital’s reception. Police filed a case under various sections against 17 persons.

Article Title: Trio first planned to hire contract killers to eliminate Ketan Agarwal, changed plan later: Police
Article Text:
Ritesh Hange (L), a friend of Chetan Choudhary, was arrested for conspiring to murder Ketan Agarwal





PUNE: Rural Police on Monday said the accused in the Ketan Agarwal murder case had initially considered hiring contract killers to eliminate him before changing the plan.Ketan (26), a builder from Gahunje, was allegedly pushed off Lohagad Fort by his fiancée Siya Goyal (20) and her boyfriend Chetan Chaudhary (22) on June 18.Superintendent of police (Pune Rural) Sandeep Singh Gill said, “The latest arrested accused, Ritesh Hange (22), played a part in the conspiracy. His role was established after we cracked the deleted messages during the digital forensic analysis.”Hange, arrested on Friday night, is accused of being part of the conspiracy with key accused Chetan and Siya, who are currently in judicial custody. “The deleted messages revealed that Ritesh and Chetan were classmates during their MBA course. They had discussed various ways to eliminate Ketan. After deliberations, they considered hiring contract killers. Ritesh later backed out of the plan,” Gill said.According to the SP, Siya and Chetan subsequently abandoned the idea of involving outsiders and decided to execute the murder themselves. “Investigations revealed that Chetan and Ritesh had initially discussed causing ‘body harm’ to Ketan. Their conversations later progressed to eliminating him, and they began considering hiring someone to carry out the murder,” Gill said.Before arresting Ritesh, police cross-verified his statements with witness accounts and technical evidence. Investigators said Ritesh had deleted chat messages and call logs to avoid suspicion, but forensic experts successfully recovered the data. “The recovered digital evidence revealed his involvement in the conspiracy,” Gill said.Police are now trying to establish Ritesh’s exact whereabouts on the day of the murder and determine whether he had any role at the crime scene. “We are studying technical evidence, including cellphone location data and CCTV footage, to establish his location on June 18,” Gill said.Investigators have also found that Chetan contacted Ritesh immediately after the murder. “Chetan met Ritesh immediately after murdering Ketan. Ritesh was the first person Chetan called after the murder,” Gill added.
Article Summary: Ketan (26), a builder from Gahunje, was allegedly pushed off Lohagad Fort by his fiancée Siya Goyal (20) and her boyfriend Chetan Chaudhary (22) on June 18. Ritesh Hange, arrested on Friday night, is accused of being part of the conspiracy with key accused Chetan and Siya.

Article Title: Noida PG operator killed after spat over loud music, two brothers held
Article Text:
(AI image used) A paying guest operator died after a loud music dispute





NOIDA: A 45-year-old paying guest (PG) accommodation operator died after allegedly being pushed during a dispute over loud music at a birthday party in Gejha of Sector 93 around 7pm on Friday. Police said two brothers were arrested and a case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder was registered at Phase 2 station.Satish Sharma, a Gejha resident, had gone to a neighbour’s house in lane number 5 to ask them to lower the volume of a home theatre system playing loud music for a birthday party. The request led to an argument with the hosts, Lalit Sharma and Sumit Sharma.Police said the confrontation escalated as Sharma was leaving after the exchange. The brothers allegedly chased and pushed him, and he fell onto the road, suffering head and facial injuries. He lost consciousness soon after and was rushed to a hospital by his family, where he was declared dead.A preliminary inquiry indicated the fatal injuries resulted from the fall following the push. Police have registered a case on the complaint of Satish’s family and arrested the two accused on Saturday.Investigators are questioning neighbours and others present at the time to establish the sequence of events, and further action will depend on the autopsy report and evidence gathered during the probe.The incident led to tension between the two sides in the locality, but police reached the spot and took steps to prevent further escalation.
Article Summary: Satish Sharma, a Gejha resident, had gone to a neighbour’s house in lane number 5 to ask them to lower the volume of a home theatre system playing loud music for a birthday party. The request led to an argument with the hosts, Lalit Sharma and Sumit Sharma. Police said the confrontation escalated as Sharma was leaving after the exchange. The brothers allegedly chased and pushed him, and he fell onto the road, suffering head and facial injuries.

Article Title: Angry MPSC aspirants warn of Jantar Mantar-like stir if govt fails to act in 3 days
Article Text:
Carrying placards and raising slogans in Pune, the protesters marched from Omkareshwar Chowk to the collectorate, halting traffic on several arterial roads.

Jantar Mantar-like protest





PUNE: Hundreds of aspirants took to the streets across Maharashtra on Monday, demanding the resignation of Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) chairman and secretary, a high-level probe into the alleged irregularities in the commission’s drug inspector examination case and that the preliminary inquiry report submitted by Mumbai crime branch be made public.The protesters warned of a Jantar Mantar-like protest if the state govt did not act on their demands in three days. The agitation came in the wake of the alleged paper leak in the MPSC Drug Inspector examination and the arrest of officials linked to the commission’s confidential section.Carrying placards and raising slogans in Pune, the protesters marched from Omkareshwar Chowk to the collectorate, halting traffic on several arterial roads. In Kolhapur, the agitators marched under the umbrella of ‘All Competitive Exams Students Action Committee’ from Dasara Chowk to the collectorate.Protesters sat on the road outside Pune collectorate while a delegation submitted a memorandum to the district administration.“We have studied for years, but are forced to stand on the roads with placards. If govt does not accept our demands, we will intensify the agitation.Our futures cannot be put at risk because of irregularities in the examination system,” Nitin Andhale, student representative and organiser of the protest, said.The aspirants also demanded a forensic audit of all MPSC examinations conducted during the tenure of officials working in the commission’s confidential section who are facing scrutiny in the paper leak case and an inquiry into their service records, promotions and the criteria used for their appointments and promotions.They also want an investigation into the suspected network involved in the paper leak, a scrutiny of financial transactions, call records, digital evidence and the contact network of the suspects.Aspirant Sumit Jadhav said, “We want an independent inquiry into doubts surrounding the results of other MPSC examinations. We need an explanation from the commission in eight days on objections raised by candidates regarding the Group B examination and a govt inquiry into whether any irregularity had occurred.”Protester Asmita Kale said students also want an inquiry into errors noticed during evaluation of descriptive answer sheets for State Services Main Examination 2025 and agriculture services examination and into alleged irregularities in the departmental examinations conducted by the state excise department and for police sub-inspectors.Youth Congress leader Akshay Jain said young people should be holding question papers not protest placards. “We need transparency, accountability and action against those responsible,” he said. Others said they would press for regular public updates on the investigation.MPSC chairman Vivek Bhimanwar said his statement on Sept 2, 2026 clarified that the drug inspector exam paper leak happened before he joined yet repeated allegations are being made against him about it.He said the commission filed a police complaint immediately and the investigation is underway. The commission and the govt have formed high-level committees and started consultations with students, parents and teachers at the divisional level.Bhimanwar said he was deeply distressed by the continued personal and politically motivated allegations against him. He added that he introduced several reforms in MPSC and conducted 84 examinations, including eight competitive examinations and 76 screening examinations for direct recruitment.Several improvements made it possible to declare results between 18 and 21 days from the time govt sought recruitment and plans are to declare other results within a month.
Article Summary: Hundreds of aspirants took to the streets across Maharashtra on Monday. The agitation came in the wake of the alleged paper leak in the MPSC Drug Inspector examination and the arrest of officials linked to the commission’s confidential section. The protesters warned of a Jantar Mantar-like protest if the state govt did not act on their demands.

Article Title: Shiv Sena Palghar city chief held for attack on hospital staffer, suspended by party
Article Text:
Palghar Shiv Sena chief Rahul Gharat allegedly assaulted a hospital employee last Saturday





PALGHAR: Deputy chief minister and Shiv Sena chief Eknath Shinde has taken serious cognisance of the alleged assault on a private hospital employee by Shiv Sena workers in Palghar.Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat, who was allegedly involved in the incident, was arrested on Monday and subsequently suspended from the party. Shinde said such incidents would not be tolerated and warned that strict action would be taken against anyone found responsible.Indian Medical Association’s Maharashtra unit has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis seeking a “fair” and “time-bound investigation” into the incident. Doctors want prompt prosecution of those found responsible as well as protection against political or external interference.The state IMA, along with IMA Boisar, has also sought stronger police-response mechanisms for healthcare establishments across Maharashtra as well as a 24x7 emergency helpline for doctors and hospitals facing violence or threats. “Healthcare professionals cannot function effectively when working under fear or intimidation,” the letter added.The incident occurred at Relief Hospital in Palghar on Saturday night over the treatment of five injured govindas.Shiv Sena workers allegedly created a ruckus at the hospital and assaulted an employee, Vivek Zinga. The party functionaries allegedly abused and threatened hospital staff before taking away the injured govindas while they were undergoing treatment.The incident has drawn widespread criticism across the state. Palghar police registered a case against 17 people, including the Shiv Sena district chief and city chief. Gharat appeared before the police on Monday and was arrested. He was produced before a court and remanded in police custody for a day. Police said efforts were on to trace the remaining accused.Reacting to the incident, Shinde said the party had suspended Gharat. “The incident is extremely unfortunate. Assaulting doctors or other healthcare workers is not justified. Shiv Sena will not support such acts,” he said.“If there was any wrongdoing in the treatment of the patients, a complaint should have been lodged through legal channels. Taking the law into one’s own hands is not acceptable, and Shiv Sena will not support it,” Shinde said.He warned party workers that violence against doctors or healthcare workers would not be tolerated under any circumstances and that those found guilty would face strict action.Meanwhile, one of the injured govindas, Akash Patil, repeated his allegations against the doctors. He claimed that although he felt better after being given an injection, he was allegedly put on a saline drip and kept in the ICU for three hours against his wishes.Palghar MLA Rajendra Gavit visited the police station and demanded that a case be registered against the doctors. He alleged that hospital staff were forcibly keeping the injured Govindas at the hospital and asking them to undergo MRI and CT scans.Gavit said Shiv Sena office-bearers had gone to the hospital to help the injured govindas and that a verbal altercation had taken place. He alleged that the doctors subsequently lodged a complaint out of vendetta and pressured the police to register a case.The injured govindas had only questioned the doctors about why they had charged an excessive bill. Gavit demanded that a case be registered against the doctors for allegedly confining the patients against their will.IMA added that an FIR should be registered under all applicable provisions, including the Maharashtra Medicare Service Persons and Medicare Service Institutions (Prevention of Violence and Damage or Loss of Property) Act, 2010, besides relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
Article Summary: Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat was arrested on Monday and subsequently suspended from the party. Indian Medical Association’s Maharashtra unit has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis. Doctors want prompt prosecution of those found responsible as well as protection against political or external interference.

Article Title: Bombay HC frees man given death for ’16 physio rape-murder
Article Text:
Bombay HC

Held from Bengal

TOI





MUMBAI: The Bombay High Court on Monday set aside death penalty awarded to a man (then 29) for the rape and murder of a 24-year-old physiotherapist in December 2016.“The finding of conviction and resultantly the imposition of death sentence upon respondent Debashish Dhara, imposed by judgement dated Oct 4, 2019, by the additional sessions judge is set aside,’’ said Justices Bharati Dangre and Manjusha Deshpande, adding that Dhara “is set at liberty. ”The state had moved HC for confirmation of the death sentence. Additional sessions judge A D Deo had found Dhara guilty of several charges, including murder, rape, unnatural sexual offences and house trespass. Dhara used to work in a jewellery store near the victim’s residence and was caught almost two months later from West Bengal.According to the prosecution, the incident occurred on the intervening night of Dec 5 and 6, 2016. The victim stayed with her family in a Mumbai suburb chawl. There was a separate mezzanine room in front of the house above a toilet. It was used for her studies and as a bedroom. On Dec 5, the victim returned home from work around 10pm. After dinner, she went into the room as usual. Around 3am, a neighbour knocked on the parents’ door and informed them about smoke coming from the victim’s room which was bolted from outside.They opened the door and found smoke everywhere and clothes and books burning. After extinguishing the fire, they found their daughter lying on the floor with jeans wrapped around her neck. Police took her to a hospital which opined she was “brought dead.” The postmortem report stated there was forcible sexual intercourse on the victim and she died due to strangulation.The trial judge noted that the crime fell in the “rarest of rare category” for the “gruesome, ghastly or horrendous act” of the accused executed with “extreme mental perversion not worthy of human condonation.”Advocate Yug Chaudhry, for Dhara, argued that prosecution’s case was based on circumstantial evidence and Dhara was implicated on suspicion. Prosecutor Tanveer Khan supported the trial court’s verdict. Advocate Siddharth Jagushte, representing the victim’s father, toldthe family will consider challenging the verdict before the Supreme Court
Article Summary: Bombay High Court sets aside death penalty awarded to a man for rape and murder. Debashish Dhara was found guilty of murder, rape, unnatural sexual offences and house trespass. Dhara used to work in a jewellery store near the victim’s residence.

Article Title: Ticketless woman held in Bihar with 75 litres of liquor in first AC coach; calm composure stuns cops
Article Text:
In photo: The arrested 25-yearold Neha Jha





PATNA: She did not become the subject of a viral video on a stage or through a social-media reel. Instead, 25-year-old Neha Jha drew attention after railway officials opened the door of a locked First AC compartment at Samastipur Junction and allegedly found her with a consignment of foreign liquor. The police interaction that followed was recorded on camera and later circulated widely on social media.What caught viewers’ attention was Neha’s apparent composure during the interaction. Speaking to the officials in fluent English and maintaining a calm demeanour, she appeared unfazed even as the compartment was being searched. The episode, however, has since become a police case involving alleged illegal transportation of liquor.Neha had travelled around 1,100km from New Delhi to Bihar in the H-1 First AC coach with her relative Ishan Kumar. The berth was booked in Ishan’s name, while police alleged that Neha was travelling without a ticket.When the train stopped at Samastipur Junction, RPF and GRP personnel reached the compartment and found the door locked from inside. After repeated knocks, Neha opened the door. The interaction was recorded by the officials.A subsequent search allegedly led to the recovery of around 75 litres of foreign liquor, estimated to be worth about Rs1.5 lakh. Neha and Ishan were arrested and later sent to judicial custody.Neha is from Bari village under Singhia police station area in Darbhanga. She is the youngest of four sisters and is reported to be a graduate of KS College in Darbhanga. She spent part of her education in Darbhanga, where police are now examining her contacts as part of their investigation into the alleged destination of the liquor.Her family background has also come under scrutiny. According to police sources, her father, Sanjay Kumar Jha, was arrested in a liquor-related case nearly two years ago. Her elder sister Nishu Jha was arrested by the excise department on Nov 30, 2025, after she was allegedly found carrying 21 litres of foreign liquor.The family also has two sons. One is still studying in school, while the other reportedly underwent treatment at a de-addiction centre in Muzaffarpur after developing a drug habit following failure in the NEET.Birbal Kumar, SHO of Rail Samastipur and the investigating officer, said, “During initial questioning, Neha reportedly claimed that she was transporting the liquor from Haryana for a wedding that will take place at her home in Dec.” An FIR was filed against Neha and Ishan under Prohibition Act, said the SHO.Police are verifying the claim and investigating whether the stated reason was genuine or was being used to explain the alleged transportation of the liquor.The investigation has now moved beyond the train compartment. Police have seized the mobile phones of Neha and Ishan and are examining their call detail records and WhatsApp conversations. Sources said Neha’s phone contained numbers belonging to several doctors and prominent businessmen in Darbhanga. Investigators are examining the conversations and contacts to determine whether any of them are linked to the alleged movement of liquor.
Article Summary: 25-year-old Neha Jha drew attention after railway officials opened the door of a locked First AC compartment at Samastipur Junction. The police interaction that followed was recorded on camera and later circulated widely on social media. Neha had travelled around 1,100km from New Delhi to Bihar in the H-1 First AC coach with her relative Ishan Kumar.
